newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Korea Development Bank l-term AA minus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Korea Development Bank l-term AA minus.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned ratings to The Korea Development Bank for the first time.
IBCA assigned a short-term A1 plus, a long-term AA minus, an individual of B/C and a legal rating of 1, it said in a statement.
"Korea Development Bank (KDB) is Korea's premier bank, playing an important role in mobilising funds to promote the long-term development of Korean industry," IBCA said.
"The necessary funds are raised on a long-term basis through the issue of bonds in domestic and international markets."
IBCA said the financial condition of KDB was sound.
"Its profitability is not high but profits are not its primary aim, which is to promote the economic development of Korea," the agency said.
IBCA said the quality of KDB's loan book was good, albeit somewhat concentrated on large borrowers in key industrial sectors, including utilities and infrastructure.
"The bank's financial condition is reflected in the Individual rating of B/C," it said.
But is added that the case of KDB, the credit ratings assigned were "predicated upon the support of the Korean authorities, rather than on the bank's condition".

"The KDB is wholly-owned by the government of Korea and, while its liabilities are not specifically guaranteed by the state, the KDB Law in effect requires that the government maintain the bank's solvency by absorbing any losses that cannot be covered by the bank's own reserves," IBCA said.
